# Asmar Nadeem

> Asmar Nadeem is Founding Technical Staff at ManaMind, where he has worked since June 2026. Previously, he was a Research Fellow in Multimodal and Spatial AI at CVSSP, University of Surrey. He completed his PhD at CVSSP, University of Surrey. His research spans causal and temporal video reasoning, video captioning, audio-visual question answering, and multimodal language models. He is the first author of Causal-VLM (NeurIPS 2026), NarrativeBridge (ICLR 2025), CAD (WACV 2024), and SEM-POS (CVPR Workshops 2023).

## Profile

## Selected publications

- [Causal-VLM: Dense Causal Captioning in Videos](https://causalvlm.github.io/). Asmar Nadeem, Mahrukh Awan, Muhammad Awais, Robert Dawes, Adrian Hilton, Armin Mustafa. NeurIPS 2026. Causal-VLM generates event captions, timestamps, and a graph of observed prerequisite relationships in long videos. It introduces the Dense Causal Captions (DCC) benchmark built on ActivityNet and YouCook2. Paper: https://causalvlm.github.io/assets/paper/Causal-VLM.pdf. Code: https://github.com/causalvlm/CausalVLM. Model weights: https://huggingface.co/causalvlm/CausalVLM. DCC labels: https://huggingface.co/datasets/causalvlm/DCC

- [NarrativeBridge: Enhancing Video Captioning with Causal-Temporal Narrative](https://openreview.net/forum?id=bBoetBIN2R). Asmar Nadeem, Faegheh Sardari, Robert Dawes, Sameed Husain, Adrian Hilton, Armin Mustafa. ICLR 2025. Existing video captioning models describe what happens but not why. NarrativeBridge contributes the Causal-Temporal Narrative (CTN) benchmark, with the MSVD-CTN and MSR-VTT-CTN datasets whose captions encode cause and effect over time, and the Cause-Effect Network (CEN), a two stream architecture that encodes cause and effect dynamics separately before decoding a causally grounded caption. Project page: https://narrativebridge.github.io/. Code: https://github.com/asmarnadeem/NarrativeBridge

- [CAD: Contextual Multi-Modal Alignment for Dynamic AVQA](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2024/papers/Nadeem_CAD_-_Contextual_Multi-Modal_Alignment_for_Dynamic_AVQA_WACV_2024_paper.pdf). Asmar Nadeem, Adrian Hilton, Robert Dawes, Graham Thomas, Armin Mustafa. WACV 2024. An end to end network for audio-visual question answering that aligns audio and visual signals at three levels: a parameter free stochastic contextual block for spatial alignment, a self supervised pre-training step for temporal alignment, and cross attention for semantic balancing. It improves over prior state of the art on the MUSIC-AVQA dataset by 9.4 percent on average. Code: https://github.com/asmarnadeem/CAD

- [SEM-POS: Grammatically and Semantically Correct Video Captioning](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023W/MULA/papers/Nadeem_SEM-POS_Grammatically_and_Semantically_Correct_Video_Captioning_CVPRW_2023_paper.pdf). Asmar Nadeem, Adrian Hilton, Robert Dawes, Graham Thomas, Armin Mustafa. CVPR Workshops 2023. A global local fusion network that supervises captioning with distinct part of speech components, aligning visual features with language structure to produce captions that are grammatically and semantically correct on the MSVD and MSR-VTT benchmarks.

## Other publications

- [Attend-Fusion: Efficient Audio-Visual Fusion for Video Classification](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-93806-1_15). Mahrukh Awan, Asmar Nadeem, Muhammad Junaid Awan, Armin Mustafa, Sameed Husain. ECCV Workshops 2024 (Springer LNCS). A compact audio-visual fusion model that captures audio-visual relationships at a fraction of the parameters of larger fusion models.
- Efficient Audio-Visual Fusion for Video Classification. Mahrukh Awan, Asmar Nadeem, Armin Mustafa. European Conference on Visual Media Production (CVMP) 2024.
- Towards Efficient Structured Description Generation for Data Marketplace Offerings. Mahrukh Awan, Asmar Nadeem, Juan Ramon Santana, Pablo Sotres, and colleagues. IEEE Conference on Standards for Communications and Networking (CSCN) 2025.
- ForecasterFlexOBM: A Multi-View Audio-Visual Dataset for Flexible Object-Based Media Production. Davide Berghi, Craig Cieciura, Farshad Einabadi, and colleagues, including Asmar Nadeem. IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo (ICME) 2024.
- HumanMoveVQA: Can Video MLLMs Reason About Human Movement in Videos? Pranav Gera, Faegheh Sardari, Asmar Nadeem, Adrian Hilton, Armin Mustafa. Preprint, 2026.

## Datasets and benchmarks

- Dense Causal Captions (DCC): event captions, temporal intervals, and observed prerequisite relationships for videos from ActivityNet and YouCook2. Released with Causal-VLM (NeurIPS 2026). Labels: https://huggingface.co/datasets/causalvlm/DCC

- Causal-Temporal Narrative (CTN) Benchmark: two video captioning datasets, MSVD-CTN and MSR-VTT-CTN, whose captions explicitly encode cause and effect temporal relationships. Released with NarrativeBridge (ICLR 2025). Details at https://narrativebridge.github.io/

## Research code

- Causal-VLM and DCC, Python: https://github.com/causalvlm/CausalVLM
- NarrativeBridge (Cause-Effect Network), Python: https://github.com/asmarnadeem/NarrativeBridge
- CAD (Contextual Multi-Modal Alignment), Python: https://github.com/asmarnadeem/CAD

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Who is Asmar Nadeem?
A: Asmar Nadeem is Founding Technical Staff at ManaMind, where he has worked since June 2026. Previously, he was a Research Fellow in Multimodal and Spatial AI at CVSSP, University of Surrey. He completed his PhD at CVSSP, University of Surrey. His research spans causal and temporal video reasoning, video captioning, audio-visual question answering, and multimodal language models.

Q: What are Asmar Nadeem's main research areas?
A: Multimodal learning, video understanding, causal and temporal reasoning, audio-visual question answering, video captioning, vision-language models, multimodal large language models, and spatial AI.

Q: What is Causal-VLM?
A: Causal-VLM, presented at NeurIPS 2026, generates event captions, timestamps, and a graph of observed prerequisite relationships in long videos. It introduces the Dense Causal Captions (DCC) benchmark, extending ActivityNet and YouCook2 with causal annotations. The project page provides the paper, code, model weights, and DCC labels. Project page: https://causalvlm.github.io/

Q: What is NarrativeBridge?
A: NarrativeBridge (ICLR 2025), led by Asmar Nadeem, is a video captioning method that describes not only what happens in a video but why. It contributes the Causal-Temporal Narrative benchmark (MSVD-CTN and MSR-VTT-CTN) and the Cause-Effect Network, a two stream architecture that models cause and effect dynamics separately before decoding a causally grounded caption.

Q: What is the Causal-Temporal Narrative (CTN) benchmark?
A: The CTN benchmark, introduced with NarrativeBridge, is a pair of video captioning datasets (MSVD-CTN and MSR-VTT-CTN) whose captions explicitly encode the cause and effect relationships between events over time, enabling evaluation of causal and temporal reasoning in video captioning.

Q: What is CAD and how does it improve audio-visual question answering?
A: CAD (Contextual Multi-Modal Alignment for Dynamic AVQA), by Asmar Nadeem and colleagues at WACV 2024, aligns audio and visual signals at the spatial, temporal, and semantic levels using a parameter free contextual block, a self supervised temporal alignment step, and cross attention. It improves over prior state of the art on the MUSIC-AVQA dataset by 9.4 percent on average.

Q: What is SEM-POS?
A: SEM-POS (CVPR Workshops 2023) is a video captioning method by Asmar Nadeem and colleagues. It uses a global local fusion network supervised with distinct part of speech components to produce captions that are both grammatically and semantically correct, reaching state of the art on MSVD and MSR-VTT.

Q: What is Attend-Fusion?
A: Attend-Fusion (ECCV Workshops 2024), with Asmar Nadeem as a co-author, is a compact audio-visual fusion model for video classification that captures audio-visual relationships at a fraction of the parameters of larger fusion approaches.

Q: What venues has Asmar Nadeem published in?
A: NeurIPS, ICLR, WACV, CVPR Workshops, ECCV Workshops, IEEE ICME, CVMP, and IEEE CSCN.

Q: Where can I find Asmar Nadeem's code and papers?
A: Code is on GitHub at github.com/asmarnadeem, including NarrativeBridge and CAD. Causal-VLM and DCC code is at https://github.com/causalvlm/CausalVLM. Publications are listed on his website at asmarnadeem.github.io, on Google Scholar, and on DBLP, with links to the published proceedings, project pages, and research code.

BibTeX entries for Causal-VLM, NarrativeBridge, CAD, and SEM-POS are on the website at https://asmarnadeem.github.io/
